name: Landmarks
description: Eight landmark roles that identify major sections of a page, helping assistive technology users understand page structure typically conveyed visually.

roles.description: Site-wide header, typically containing logo and nav. Use <header> (not inside <article>/<section>)
Primary content. Use <main>. Only one per page
Content related but separate from main. Use <aside>
A form when it has an accessible name. Use <form> with aria-label/aria-labelledby
A perceivable section with accessible name. Use <section> with aria-label/aria-labelledby
Search facility. Use <search> element or role='search'

required_attributes.description: Unique accessible name to distinguish multiple landmarks of same type

notes: Use the native elements. <nav> IS role='navigation'; adding role='navigation' to it is redundant noise.
Exactly ONE <main> per page. It is the target of the skip link (RAWeb 12.7).
<header>/<footer> only map to banner/contentinfo when they are NOT nested inside <article>, <aside>, <main>, <nav> or <section>. A <header> inside an <article> is just a header.
Several landmarks of the same type must be told apart with aria-label: <nav aria-label='Main'> and <nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'>.
Do not put the landmark type in the label: <nav aria-label='Main navigation'> is announced 'Main navigation navigation'. Say 'Main'.
<section> is only a landmark (role='region') when it has an accessible name. An unnamed <section> is a generic div as far as AT is concerned.
Do not wrap the whole page in landmarks. If everything is a landmark, the landmark list is useless — it exists to let users skip TO things.

raweb_criteria.reason: THE criterion for this pattern. The document structure must be consistent — landmarks are how that structure is exposed to assistive technologies.
Content grouping blocks repeated across pages (header, nav, footer) must be reachable or bypassable — landmarks are the mechanism.
A skip link to the main content region is required. It needs a <main> to skip TO.
Where several landmarks of the same type exist, each needs a distinguishing accessible name.
